Based on the document provided, I can only identify information related to **reprisal protections** for tenants. The document does not contain information about the other rental housing obligations and exemptions you've asked about.

Here is what the document covers:

**Reprisal Protections (Enacted)**

citations.cited_text: Any person or agent thereof who threatens to or takes reprisals against any tenant of residential premises for the tenant's act of, commencing, proceeding with, or obtaining relief in any judicial or administrative action the purpose of which action is to obtain damages under, or otherwise enforce, any federal, state or local law, regulation, by-law or ordinance, which has as its objective the regulation of residential premises; or exercising the tenant's rights pursuant to section one hundred and twenty-four D of chapter one hundred and sixty-four; or reporting to the board of health or, in the city of Boston to the commissioner of housing inspection or to any other board having as its objective the regulation of residential premises a violation or a suspected violation of any health or building code or of any other municipal by-law or ordinance, or state or federal law or regulation which has as its objective the regulation of residential premises; or reporting or complaining of such violation or suspected violation in writing to the landlord or to the agent of the landlord; or for organizing or joining a tenants' union or similar organization, or for making or expressing an intention to make, a payment of rent to an organization of unit owners pursuant to paragraph (c) of section six of chapter one hundred and eighty-three A shall be liable for damages which shall not be less than one month's rent or more than three month's rent, or the actual damages sustained by the tenant, whichever is greater, and the costs of the suit, including a reasonable attorney's fee.

content.text: Landlords or their agents are prohibited from threatening or taking reprisals against tenants for: commencing judicial or administrative actions to enforce federal, state, or local laws regulating residential premises; exercising tenant rights; reporting violations of health or building codes to boards of health or other regulatory bodies; reporting or complaining about violations in writing to the landlord; or organizing or joining tenants' unions.

citations.cited_text: Any person or agent thereof who threatens to or takes reprisals against any tenant of residential premises for the tenant's act of, commencing, proceeding with, or obtaining relief in any judicial or administrative action the purpose of which action is to obtain damages under, or otherwise enforce, any federal, state or local law, regulation, by-law or ordinance, which has as its objective the regulation of residential premises; or exercising the tenant's rights pursuant to section one hundred and twenty-four D of chapter one hundred and sixty-four; or reporting to the board of health or, in the city of Boston to the commissioner of housing inspection or to any other board having as its objective the regulation of residential premises a violation or a suspected violation of any health or building code or of any other municipal by-law or ordinance, or state or federal law or regulation which has as its objective the regulation of residential premises; or reporting or complaining of such violation or suspected violation in writing to the landlord or to the agent of the landlord; or for organizing or joining a tenants' union or similar organization, or for making or expressing an intention to make, a payment of rent to an organization of unit owners pursuant to paragraph (c) of section six of chapter one hundred and eighty-three A shall be liable for damages which shall not be less than one month's rent or more than three month's rent, or the actual damages sustained by the tenant, whichever is greater, and the costs of the suit, including a reasonable attorney's fee.

content.text: Violations result in liability for damages of not less than one month's rent or more than three months' rent (or actual damages, whichever is greater), plus costs of suit including reasonable attorney's fees.

citations.cited_text: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action, exercised such rights, made such report or complaint, or organized or joined such tenants' union or within six months after any other person has taken such action or actions on behalf of the tenant or in, or relating to, the building in which the tenant resides, shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities.

content.text: A rebuttable presumption of reprisal is created if a notice of termination (except for nonpayment of rent), rent increase, or substantial alteration in tenancy terms is received within six months after protected tenant activities.

citations.cited_text: Any waiver of this provision in any lease or other rental agreement shall be void and unenforceable.

content.text: Any waiver of these protections in leases or rental agreements is void and unenforceable.
The document does not contain information about rent caps, just cause eviction standards, deposit rules, application/screening fees, screening restrictions, or algorithmic pricing.
